Marcus, thank you for this exit interview. I really want to understand why you decided to switch.
Honestly, it was the budget cut. In June our finance team cut the software budget by thirty percent.
We did not know that. If we had known about the budget, we would have offered you a smaller plan.
Maybe. But the competitor offered a big discount, and our CFO saw it first.
Was the price the deal-breaker, or was there something else?
The price was the turning point. But if your team had called us in the spring, we wouldn't have looked at other vendors.
That is fair. The lesson learned for us is clear: talk to finance, not only to the users.
I appreciate that. And if your pricing changes, call me. We did not walk away forever.
If anything changes on your side, we would love a second chance.

Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. Thank you for doing the Harbor Health exit interview. I know it is not a nice call. Before you write the report, remember why we do this. A lost account is expensive, but a lost lesson is more expensive. So please write it with the third conditional, and be specific. Not: if we had worked harder, we would have kept them. That helps nobody. Write something like: if we had seen the budget cut in June, we would have offered a smaller plan. One condition, one result, one date. And please end with one thing that we will do differently from next month. Send it to me by Friday, and we will present it together at the team meeting.

Hi Patrícia, it is Tom. Karen told me about Harbor Health. I am sorry, I know how that feels. Last year I lost a logistics account in almost the same way. Their director changed in March, and nobody on my side noticed. If I had met the new director in the first month, I would have kept the account, I am sure. Since then, I have a simple rule: every time a sponsor changes, I book a meeting within two weeks. It takes one hour, and it has saved two renewals. Anyway, if you want a second pair of eyes on your report, send it to me before Friday. Happy to help.
